why: Step 1 PASSES: the quoted sentence exists verbatim at channels-reference.md:463, and the whole line plus the two lines around it (:474 'The verdict your server sends back is notifications/claude/channel/permission with two fields: request_id ... and behavior', :199 the capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'] row) confirm rather than reverse the claimed behaviour. Step 2 PASSES on substance, drifts on the cite: grep -ran 'channel/permission' over source returns nothing (positive control: the same grep for 'claude/channel' DOES find the sibling half at packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:113, config/storage.ts:95, mcp/mcp-pool.ts, so the grep works and the absence is real); grep -ran 'notifications/claude' over packages+apps is likewise empty. The cited packages/core/src/types/message.ts:962 is off by 13 lines (permission_request is at :975, permission_request_cancelled at :989; :962 is a comment header), and the claimed evidence '0 hits' is literally false as written -- the same command returns 16 hits, all of them the sweep's own rows in docs/superpowers/specs/. Step 3 REFUTES the finding on its consequence, which is the exact shape 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md sec.4 item 3 warns about ('the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something else already handles it' -- and its example is also a channel row). The finding asserts 'a paused session cannot be unblocked remotely'. That is false: Nessy's own wire protocol relays every permission prompt to every connected client and accepts the verdict back from any of them. packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:377-378 carries permission_request / permission_request_cancelled as server events; RPC_CHANNELS.sessions.RESPOND_TO_PERMISSION (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:38) is handled at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:462 and, decisively, is a member of REMOTE_ELIGIBLE_CHANNELS (packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts:242 declares the set, :283 lists RESPOND_TO_PERMISSION) -- so apps/cli attached to a remote nessy-server can answer a paused session's prompt over the network. A remote-approval path exists; the MCP-channel-shaped one does not. Second, the 'channel plugin' framing names an already-recorded deferral rather than a new gap: a plugin's channels field is a deliberately retained-but-deferred surface (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2271, { externalKind: 'channel', field: 'channels' } -> reasonCode plugin.deferred.claude_channel), and the deviation register already records it ('channels are still a wholly deferred surface here', 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:264), which is the one deviation the coverage map counts for this page (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:127). Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist sec.3, and not a rebrand/subscription-drop product difference. Adjacent, and bigger than f137 but out of its scope: our inbound half does not match the page's wire contract either -- client.ts:113 registers z.literal('claude/channel') and reads params.text, while channels-reference.md:236 specifies method 'notifications/claude/channel' with params { content, meta }.
correctedState: The permission-relay half is genuinely absent: no source file mentions channel/permission or any notifications/claude method, nothing declares capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'], nothing emits notifications/claude/channel/permission_request and nothing accepts a notifications/claude/channel/permission verdict. But the finding's stated consequence is wrong on both clauses. (1) 'A paused session cannot be unblocked remotely' is false -- permission prompts travel to every connected client as protocol/dto.ts:377 permission_request events and the answer comes back on sessions:respondToPermission, which routing.ts:283 places in REMOTE_ELIGIBLE_CHANNELS and server-core/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:462 handles, so a remote CLI can unblock the session today; what is missing is relay to a third-party chat app, not remote approval. (2) 'A channel plugin gets no prompts' understates and mis-scopes: a plugin-declared channels component is not loaded at all here -- it is a deliberately deferred surface (format-adapters/claude.ts:2271, plugin.deferred.claude_channel) already recorded in the deviation register (:264) -- so such a plugin gets no channel messages either, and the relay is a sub-item of that recorded deferral. The relay gap is real only for a directly configured MCP server, where the inbound push half does exist (client.ts:113, gated by mcpChannelPushEnabled, default false, and by managed channelsEnabled). Cite drift: the internal event type is message.ts:975, not :962, and the 'grep -> 0 hits' evidence returns 16 hits, all in the sweep's own docs.
